mainTopic: פורים gifts, drinking and the פורים meal; the differences between יום טוב, שבת and יום הכפורים
overview: This amud opens with stories about פורים gifts. רבי אושעיא thanks רבי יהודה נשיאה for a gift that counted as both משלוח מנות and מתנות לאביונים. Next, רבה and מרי בר מר trade gifts through אביי, who describes a huge meal. Then רבא says a person must drink on פורים until he cannot tell 'cursed is המן' from 'blessed is מרדכי'. The next story, about רבה and רבי זירא, shows that drinking going badly wrong. רבא also rules that a סעודת פורים eaten at night does not count, and a story with רב אשי and רב כהנא shows this rule in action. A new משנה then teaches that the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation, and the גמרא explains the debate with רבי יהודה over preparing the tools for food. Another משנה compares שבת and יום הכפורים. This leads to a discussion of whether מלקות remove כרת, where בי רב's proof from the משנה is turned back by רב נחמן and רב אשי.

steps.title: One gift fulfills two פורים מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא tells רבי יהודה נשיאה that his gift fulfilled both משלוח מנות and מתנות לאביונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You have fulfilled through us, our teacher, both "sending portions one to another" and "gifts to the poor."
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a story that began on the previous amud. רבי יהודה נשיאה had sent a gift to רבי אושעיא, and רבי אושעיא answers that this one gift counted for two מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא was poor, so a generous gift to him was more than an ordinary פורים present. It counted as משלוח מנות and also as מתנות לאביונים. He quotes the two phrases straight from the פסוק in מגילת אסתר.

keyTerms.meaning: Sending portions of food to a friend on פורים
Gifts to the poor on פורים

steps.whatToRemember: A generous gift to a poor friend can count for both משלוח מנות and מתנות לאביונים.

phrases.english: You have fulfilled through us, our teacher,
phrases.notes: רבי אושעיא is speaking to רבי יהודה נשיאה, who sent him the gift.

phrases.english: "And sending portions one to another
phrases.notes: A quote from the פסוק in מגילת אסתר (ט:כב).

phrases.english: and gifts to the poor."
phrases.notes: He counts himself as one of the poor, so the gift covers this מצוה too.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִיַּימְתָּ בָּנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the רבי יהודה נשיאה and רבי אושעיא story that began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A single generous gift to a poor person can fulfill both פורים gift מצוות at once.

steps.title: רבה sends a simple gift through אביי
steps.stepSummary: רבה sends dates and roasted flour to מרי בר מר, and אביי worries it will look too plain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה sent a sack of dates and a cup of roasted flour to מרי בר מר by way of אביי. אביי said to him: Now מרי will say, "Even if a farmer becomes king, the basket does not come off his neck."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new פורים story. רבה sends a very plain gift, and אביי, who carried it, warns that it will look cheap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה had become a great leader but was still poor, so his gift was simple. אביי quotes a popular saying: a farmer who becomes king still acts like a farmer. He worries מרי בר מר will see the gift that way.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה שַׁדַּר לֵיהּ לְמָרֵי בַּר מָר
phrases.english: Rabba sent to Marei bar Mar
in the hands of Abaye
a sack full of dates
and a cupful of roasted flour.
Abaye said to him:
Now Mari will say:
phrases.notes: "Mari" here means מרי בר מר, the one getting the gift.

phrases.english: If a farmer becomes king,
the basket does not come down from his neck.
phrases.notes: A popular saying: even with a new high position, a person keeps his old simple habits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה שַׁדַּר לֵיהּ לְמָרֵי בַּר מָר בְּיַד אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a second, separate story about משלוח מנות between חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה sent a modest משלוח מנות, and אביי worried it would be seen as too humble for a leader.

steps.title: מרי בר מר sends back a sharp-tasting gift
steps.stepSummary: מרי בר מר answers with ginger and long peppers, and אביי jokes about how רבה will take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back a sack of ginger and a cup of long peppers. אביי said: Now the master will say, "I sent him sweet things, and he sent me sharp things."
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: מרי בר מר sends a gift back to רבה. אביי again jokes about the reaction it will get.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ginger and long peppers were expensive spices, much richer than dates and flour. But they taste sharp, while רבה's gift was sweet. אביי playfully says רבה will notice the sweet-for-sharp swap.

phrases.english: He in turn sent back to him
phrases.notes: "He" is מרי בר מר, sending a gift back to רבה.

phrases.english: a sack full of ginger
and a cupful of long peppers.
Abaye said:
Now the master will say:
phrases.notes: "The master" here is רבה, אביי's teacher.

phrases.english: I sent him sweet things,
and he sent me sharp things.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר שַׁדַּר לֵיהּ אִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reply gift to the one in step 2, with a second joke from אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרי בר מר answered with a richer but sharp-tasting gift, and אביי joked about the sweet-for-sharp exchange.

steps.title: אביי describes the huge meal at מרי בר מר's house
steps.stepSummary: אביי was already full when he left רבה, yet at מרי בר מר's house he ate sixty dishes and still wanted more.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When I left the master's house, I was full. When I got there, they brought me sixty plates of sixty kinds of cooked food, and I ate sixty portions of them. The last dish was called pot roast, and I wanted to chew the plate after it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells what happened when he delivered the gift. Even though he came already full, he was served a huge meal and kept eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contrast is clear: he was full when he left רבה's house, yet he still ate sixty portions. The last dish was so good he wanted to chew the plate. The story shows how lavishly מרי בר מר hosted him.
steps.confusionAlert: "The master's house" (בי מר) here is רבה's house, where אביי started out, not מרי בר מר's house. "There" (התם) is מרי בר מר's house.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When I left the master's house,
phrases.notes: He means רבה's house, where he picked up the gift.

phrases.english: I was full.
When I arrived there,
they brought me sixty plates
of sixty kinds of cooked dishes,
and I ate sixty portions of them.
And the last dish,
they called it pot roast,
and I wanted to chew the plate after it.
phrases.notes: A way of saying the food was so good he still wanted more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי נְפַקִי מִבֵּי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי adds his own account of the same trip, describing the meal he got when he delivered רבה's gift.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Although already full, אביי ate sixty portions at מרי בר מר's house and still wanted more of the last dish.

steps.title: אביי explains his big appetite with two folk sayings
steps.stepSummary: אביי sums up his experience of eating sixty dishes after being full, using two popular proverbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what people mean when they say, 'A poor man is hungry and does not even know it.' Or another saying: 'There is always room for sweet things.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes his own story from the last step by quoting two common sayings that explain how he could eat so much after he was already full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first saying suggests that אביי was really still hungry at רבה's house without realizing it. The second suggests that good food always finds room, even in a full stomach. The words אי נמי show these are two different explanations, not one.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk saying)

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what people mean when they say:
The poor man is hungry and does not know it.
phrases.notes: He means himself. At רבה's house he thought he was full, but he was actually still hungry.

phrases.english: Alternatively: there is always room for something sweet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends אביי's story from step 4 by explaining his appetite with proverbs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two possible explanations: he was really hungry without knowing it, or tasty food always finds room.

steps.title: Two אמוראים swap their פורים meals
steps.stepSummary: אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין fulfilled משלוח מנות by exchanging their meals with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין used to swap their meals with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another short example of how אמוראים fulfilled sending food to each other on פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the fancy gifts in the earlier stories, here each one simply sent his own meal to the other. This shows a very simple way to fulfill משלוח מנות, with both sides giving and receiving.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Abaye bar Avin and Rabbi Ḥanina bar Avin
would exchange their meals with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר אָבִין מְחַלְּפִי סְעוֹדְתַּיְיהוּ לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example of משלוח מנות after the רבה and מרי בר מר stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swapping meals with one another is a way to fulfill משלוח מנות.

steps.title: רבא: drink on פורים until you can't tell המן from מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a person must drink on פורים until he does not know the difference between 'cursed is המן' and 'blessed is מרדכי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person must become drunk on פורים until he cannot tell the difference between 'cursed is המן' and 'blessed is מרדכי'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from gifts to a new topic: רבא states an obligation to drink on פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא uses the word 'obligated', so this is presented as a real requirement, not just a custom. He also sets a limit for how far it goes: until a person cannot tell the curse of המן from the blessing of מרדכי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the main source for the well-known practice of drinking on פורים, and the story right after it shapes how it is understood.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מִיחַיַּיב אִינִישׁ לְבַסּוֹמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא
phrases.english: Rava said: A person is obligated to become drunk on Purim
until he does not know
the difference between 'cursed is Haman' and 'blessed is Mordecai.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִיחַיַּיב אִינִישׁ לְבַסּוֹמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from משלוח מנות to a new פורים rule about drinking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an obligation to drink on פורים until one cannot tell 'cursed is המן' from 'blessed is מרדכי'.

steps.title: רבה and רבי זירא's פורים feast goes terribly wrong
steps.stepSummary: At a shared פורים meal, רבה and רבי זירא got drunk, רבה killed רבי זירא, and the next day he prayed and brought him back to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רבי זירא made a פורים feast together. They got drunk. רבה got up and slaughtered רבי זירא. The next day, רבה prayed for mercy and brought him back to life.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after רבא's rule about drinking, the גמרא tells a story showing how dangerous drinking on פורים can become.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Placing this story right after רבא's statement adds a warning beside the rule. The drinking led to a disaster that was fixed only through a miracle when רבה prayed.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought him back to life

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה וְרַבִּי זֵירָא עֲבַדוּ סְעוּדַת פּוּרִים בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי.
phrases.english: Rabba and Rabbi Zeira made a Purim feast together.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבַּסּוּם. קָם רַבָּה שַׁחְטֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא.
phrases.english: They became drunk. Rabba got up and slaughtered Rabbi Zeira.
The next day, he prayed for mercy and brought him back to life.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַבִּי זֵירָא עֲבַדוּ סְעוּדַת פּוּרִים בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story about drinking on פורים right after רבא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking at the פורים feast led to a disaster that was undone only by a miracle.

steps.title: רבי זירא refuses a second פורים feast
steps.stepSummary: The next year רבה invited רבי זירא again, and רבי זירא declined, saying miracles do not happen every time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year, רבה said to him: 'Come, let us make the פורים feast together.' He answered: 'A miracle does not happen every single time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי זירא turning down רבה's invitation, which gives the lesson of the whole story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא does not argue with רבה. He simply points out that he was saved only by a miracle last time. The lesson is that you should not count on a miracle to protect you from danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master come (a polite invitation)
At each and every hour; every time

steps.whatToRemember: Right next to רבא's rule to drink on פורים, the גמרא tells the story of רבה and רבי זירא, which ends with 'miracles don't happen every time.'

phrases.english: The next year, he said to him:
phrases.notes: The speaker here is רבה, inviting רבי זירא again.

phrases.aramaic: נֵיתֵי מָר וְנַעֲבֵיד סְעוּדַת פּוּרִים בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי.
phrases.english: Let the master come, and let us make the Purim feast together.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא בְּכֹל שַׁעְתָּא וְשַׁעְתָּא
phrases.english: He said to him: Not at each and every hour
does a miracle happen.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא בְּכֹל שַׁעְתָּא וְשַׁעְתָּא מִתְרְחִישׁ נִיסָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story from step 8 with רבי זירא's refusal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One should not count on a miracle to save him a second time, so רבי זירא declined to repeat the feast.

steps.title: The סעודת פורים must be eaten by day
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a סעודת פורים eaten at night does not fulfill the obligation, because the פסוק says 'days of feasting.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If someone ate the פורים meal at night, he did not fulfill his obligation. Why? Because the פסוק says 'days of feasting and gladness,' meaning days, not nights.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule: the פורים meal only counts if you eat it during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the פסוק in מגילת אסתר, 'ימי משתה ושמחה.' The word 'days' tells us the feast belongs to the daytime. So a meal on the night of פורים, even a big one, does not count for the מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה: the סעודת פורים is eaten on the day of פורים, not the night before.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A Purim feast that one ate at night
did not fulfill his obligation.
What is the reason?
"Days of feasting and gladness" is written.
phrases.notes: This is from מגילת אסתר. The key word is 'days,' so nights are left out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: סְעוּדַת פּוּרִים שֶׁאֲכָלָהּ בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פורים stories in steps 5-9, the גמרא brings another פורים meal rule from רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סעודת פורים eaten at night does not fulfill the obligation, since the פסוק says 'days.'

steps.title: רב אשי asks why the רבנן did not come to learn
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: on פורים the רבנן did not show up to learn with רב כהנא, and רב אשי asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי was sitting in front of רב כהנא. It got late and the רבנן did not come. רב אשי asked: Why didn't the רבנן come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will show רבא's rule from step 10 in action. This question sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual learning group did not come on פורים. רב אשי simply wants to know why. The answer will connect to the פורים meal.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the student in this story

phrases.english: Rav Ashi was sitting
before Rav Kahana.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, so they don't say whose presence he was in.

phrases.english: It grew dark, and the Rabbis did not come.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב אשי is asking his teacher רב כהנא.

phrases.english: What is the reason the Rabbis did not come?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows how רבא's rule was passed on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the regular learning group did not come on פורים.

steps.title: רב כהנא: They are probably busy with the סעודת פורים
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא suggests the רבנן are busy eating the סעודת פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא answered: Maybe they are busy with the פורים meal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers רב אשי's question with a guess: the רבנן are at their פורים meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer brings up the timing of the meal. It was daytime, so the meal took them away from learning. That leads straight into רב אשי's next challenge.

phrases.english: Perhaps they are busy with the Purim feast.
phrases.notes: רב כהנא is the one answering here.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא טְרִידִי בִּסְעוּדַת פּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן are busy with the daytime סעודת פורים.

steps.title: רב אשי: Couldn't they eat it at night?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges: why not eat the פורים meal at night and keep the day free for learning?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Wasn't it possible for them to eat the meal at night?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on the answer. He asks why the meal could not be moved to the night, so no learning would be lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי assumes the meal can be eaten at any time on פורים, night or day. If so, skipping learning in the day seems unnecessary. This assumption is exactly what רב כהנא will correct.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Wasn't it possible
to eat it at night?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הֲוָה אֶפְשָׁר לְמֵיכְלַהּ בְּאוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the רבנן had to miss daytime learning for the meal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the meal can be eaten at night, they should eat it then and keep learning during the day.

steps.title: רב כהנא quotes רבא: a night meal does not count
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers by quoting רבא's rule that a סעודת פורים at night does not fulfill the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to him: Didn't you hear what רבא said, that a פורים meal eaten at night does not fulfill the obligation?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge with רבא's rule from step 10. The meal has to be in the day, so they could not move it to the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's challenge depended on the night meal being enough. רבא's ruling shows it is not, so the רבנן were right to eat during the day. Here the גמרא repeats רבא's words on purpose, now to answer a question.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Has the master not heard
that which Rava said:
A Purim feast that one ate at night
did not fulfill his obligation?
phrases.notes: This is the same rule from step 10, now used to answer רב אשי.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ לְמָר הָא דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an existing ruling that removes the challenger's assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פורים meal can be eaten at night just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: A night meal does not count, so it must be eaten by day, even if that costs learning time.

steps.title: רב אשי confirms the rule and reviews it forty times
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether רבא really said this, hears 'yes,' and reviews it forty times until it is firmly his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Did רבא really say that? רב כהנא said: Yes. רב אשי learned it from him forty times, until it felt as if it was sitting in his pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב אשי checking that the rule is real and then reviewing it until he knows it perfectly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ruling is confirmed, the question is closed: the meal is by day. רב אשי's forty reviews show how seriously he took a ruling he had not known. The picture of 'in his pocket' means it was now fully his.
steps.whatToRemember: The סעודת פורים must be eaten during the day. A meal at night does not count, even if it means missing daytime learning.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Did Rava say this?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets, and others have the words in square brackets instead.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
He learned it from him forty times
and it seemed to him as if it were placed in his pocket.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא מִינֵּיהּ אַרְבְּעִין זִימְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the answer of step 14 and closes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's rule is confirmed: the פורים meal must be eaten by day.

steps.title: New משנה: The only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is that cooking food is allowed on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The only difference between יום טוב and שבת is preparing food.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It uses the same 'the only difference between' wording as the previous משנה, now comparing יום טוב and שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the work that is forbidden on שבת is also forbidden on יום טוב, except one area: preparing food, like cooking and baking. That is allowed on יום טוב and forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There is no difference between Yom Tov and Shabbat
except preparing food alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת אֶלָּא אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ בִּלְבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The פורים topic is over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only food preparation separates יום טוב from שבת; all other work is forbidden on both.

steps.title: Inference: Preparatory steps for food are forbidden on both days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads from the word 'only' that preparing the tools for food (מכשירי אוכל נפש) is forbidden on both יום טוב and שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This tells us that for the preparation steps for food, both days are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the משנה's wording, 'only food.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows only the food work itself, like cooking. Steps that just get you ready to make food, like sharpening a knife, are not the food work itself. So they stay forbidden on יום טוב just like on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Steps that prepare for making food, like fixing a tool

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up אוכל נפש, the food work itself (allowed on יום טוב), with מכשירי אוכל נפש, getting tools ready for it (here, forbidden on both days).

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that regarding things that prepare for food preparation
this and that are equal.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means שבת and יום טוב. On both, these steps are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְעִנְיַן מַכְשִׁירֵי אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the wording of the משנה in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By the משנה, מכשירי אוכל נפש are forbidden on יום טוב as on שבת.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes the משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה, who in a ברייתא allows מכשירי אוכל נפש on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches: The only difference between יום טוב and שבת is preparing food. רבי יהודה allows even the preparation steps for food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies whose view the משנה follows. It brings a ברייתא to show that רבי יהודה holds differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has the same opening line as our משנה, but adds that רבי יהודה allows the preparation steps too. Since step 17 read our משנה as forbidding those steps, our משנה must follow the רבנן and not רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught:
There is no difference between Yom Tov and Shabbat
except preparing food;
Rabbi Yehuda permits
even the preparatory steps for food.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reading in step 17 to identify whose view the משנה follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows the רבנן against רבי יהודה, who allows מכשירי אוכל נפש on יום טוב.

steps.title: What is the first opinion's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind the תנא קמא's view that מכשירי אוכל נפש are forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the first opinion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא forbids the preparations for food on יום טוב. This question sets up the next step, where the verse is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 we learned that the משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה. Now the גמרא wants to see where in the Torah each side gets its view, starting with the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a teaching

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first Tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion identified in step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind the תנא קמא's ban on מכשירי אוכל נפש

steps.title: Each side's word in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns from the word 'הוא' ('that') that only the food itself is allowed, not its preparations. רבי יהודה learns from 'לכם' ('for you') that all your needs are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'that': that itself, and not its preparations. And רבי יהודה says: 'for you' means for you, for all your needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the verse. Each side focuses on a different word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about יום טוב says 'only that may be done for you.' The תנא קמא reads 'הוא' as limiting: only making the food itself is allowed. רבי יהודה reads 'לכם' as widening: anything you need for the food, including the tools, is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Its preparations: things that make the food-making possible

phrases.english: The verse says: 'that,' and not its preparations,
phrases.notes: The פסוק is in שמות 12:16: 'only what every person eats, that alone may be done for you.'

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda (says): 'for you'
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: for you, for all your needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״הוּא״ — וְלֹא מַכְשִׁירָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 and adds רבי יהודה's source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא learns from 'הוא'; רבי יהודה learns from 'לכם'

steps.title: What does the first opinion do with 'for you'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא: the verse also says 'לכם', which seems to allow all needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't 'for you' written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא. The word 'לכם' is in the verse too, so how does he deal with it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לכם' means 'all your needs,' it seems to allow the preparations, against the תנא קמא. He must have some other reading of that word.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)

phrases.english: And the other one too, isn't 'for you' written?
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here is the תנא קמא, who forbids the preparations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הָכְתִיב ״לָכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תנא קמא using רבי יהודה's word
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse contains 'לכם', which רבי יהודה reads as allowing all needs; the תנא קמא must explain it

steps.title: 'For you': not for non-Jews or dogs
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses 'לכם' to teach that cooking on יום טוב is only for Jews, not for non-Jews or for animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For you,' and not for non-Jews; 'for you,' and not for dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the תנא קמא. He uses 'לכם' to teach a different limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, 'לכם' does not widen the rule. It narrows who the cooking may be for: only you, not non-Jews and not animals. So the word is used up, and the preparations stay forbidden.

phrases.english: For you, and not for non-Jews,
for you, and not for dogs.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָכֶם וְלֹא לְגוֹיִם, לָכֶם וְלֹא לִכְלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the word: 'לכם' narrows the people, not the actions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לכם' must mean all your needs, which would allow the preparations
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לכם' excludes non-Jews and animals, so the תנא קמא's ban on preparations stands

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with 'that'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: the verse also says 'הוא', which limits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't 'that' written?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the question on רבי יהודה. The limiting word 'הוא' is in the verse too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'הוא' means only the food itself, it seems to forbid the preparations, against רבי יהודה. He must explain what that word teaches.

phrases.english: And the other one too, isn't 'that' written?
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is רבי יהודה, who allows the preparations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הָא כְּתִיב ״הוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same kind of challenge, now aimed at the other side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse contains the limiting word 'הוא', which seems to exclude preparations

steps.title: Splitting preparations into two kinds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses both words. 'הוא' forbids preparations that could have been done before יום טוב, and 'לכם' allows preparations that could not have been done before.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'That' is written and 'for you' is written. Here it is about preparations that could be done on the day before יום טוב; there it is about preparations that could not be done on the day before יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה. He keeps both words by applying each one to a different kind of preparation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse has one limiting word and one widening word. רבי יהודה says 'הוא' forbids preparations you could have done on ערב יום טוב, and 'לכם' allows preparations you could not have done in advance. So רבי יהודה's permission is only for the second kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there: splitting two sources between two cases

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה allows every kind of preparation on יום טוב. Here he only allows preparations that could not have been done before the חג.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא: 'הוא' forbids all preparations, and 'לכם' excludes non-Jews and dogs. רבי יהודה: preparations that could not be done before יום טוב are allowed, and those that could are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the line for רבי יהודה's view: the permission depends on whether the work could have been done ahead of time.

phrases.english: 'That' is written, and 'for you' is written.
phrases.notes: One word limits and one word widens, so each must cover a different case.

phrases.english: Here, with preparations that it is possible
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the word 'הוא', which forbids.

phrases.english: to do on the day before יום טוב,
there, with preparations that it is impossible
phrases.notes: This 'there' is the word 'לכם', which allows.

phrases.english: to do on the day before יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב ״הוּא״ וּכְתִיב ״לָכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 and closes the discussion
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן): each word applies to a different kind of preparation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הוא' would forbid all preparations, against רבי יהודה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הוא' forbids preparations that could have been done before יום טוב; 'לכם' allows those that could not

steps.title: The difference between שבת and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that the only difference between שבת and יום הכפורים is the punishment for breaking them on purpose: a court punishes for שבת, and כרת is the punishment for יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difference between שבת and יום הכפורים except that for this one, breaking it on purpose is punished by people, and for that one, breaking it on purpose is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts, in the same 'the only difference between...' style. It compares שבת and יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden מלאכות are the same on both days, so even cooking is forbidden on יום הכפורים. The one difference is the punishment for doing it on purpose. On שבת a human court punishes, and on יום הכפורים the punishment is כרת, from Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: By human hands: punished by a court
Being 'cut off': a punishment from Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: 'Only the punishment is different' means the forbidden work is the same on both days. Unlike יום טוב, cooking is not allowed on יום הכפורים.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין בֵּין שַׁבָּת לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: MISHNA: There is no difference between שבת and יום הכפורים,
except that this one: its on-purpose breaking is punished by people,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is שבת. A court punishes someone who breaks it on purpose.

phrases.english: and that one: its on-purpose breaking is punished with כרת.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is יום הכפורים, where the punishment comes from Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין שַׁבָּת לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה in the same 'אין בין' series as step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת and יום הכפורים have the same forbidden מלאכות; only the punishment for breaking them on purpose differs (a court for שבת, כרת for יום הכפורים)

steps.title: שבת and יום הכפורים are equal regarding payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the משנה's wording that for paying damages, שבת and יום הכפורים are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that for paying damages, both are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the last משנה closely. If the 'only' difference is the punishment, then everything else is the same, including paying for damages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the only difference between שבת and יום הכפורים is the type of punishment. So for every other law they must be equal. That includes the rule that a person who deserves a severe punishment does not also pay for damage he did through that same act.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that with regard to payment,
phrases.notes: He means paying for damage a person causes while breaking שבת or יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: this one and that one are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְעִנְיַן תַּשְׁלוּמִין זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new conclusion from the exact wording of the משנה in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the משנה says the only difference is the punishment, שבת and יום הכפורים are equal regarding payment for damages: in both, he is exempt.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which Sage holds that יום הכפורים is like שבת regarding payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which Sage the משנה follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Treating יום הכפורים like שבת for payment is not obvious. For שבת the punishment is death by a court, but for יום הכפורים it is כרת. So the גמרא wants to know who holds this view.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is our mishna?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who holds the conclusion drawn in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that יום הכפורים is like שבת regarding the exemption from payment.

steps.title: It follows רבי נחוניא בן הקנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, who treats יום הכפורים like שבת for payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי נחוניא בן הקנה. A ברייתא teaches: he treated יום הכפורים like שבת for payment. Just as on שבת a person is liable with his life and so exempt from paying, the same is true on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, and quotes a ברייתא showing his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a person who deserves death is exempt from paying for damage done in the same act. רבי נחוניא בן הקנה says יום הכפורים works the same way, because there too he is 'liable with his life' through כרת. So he is exempt from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who compares יום הכפורים to שבת regarding payment
Liable with his life (deserves a life-taking punishment)

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana,
as it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana would make
Yom Kippur like Shabbat regarding payment:
just as on Shabbat he is liable with his life
and is exempt from payment,
so too on Yom Kippur he is liable with his life
phrases.notes: On יום הכפורים the punishment is כרת, and he counts that as 'liable with his life' too.

phrases.english: and is exempt from payment.

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי נחוניא בן הקנה: a person who deserves כרת on יום הכפורים is exempt from paying, just like on שבת.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, who compares יום הכפורים to שבת: both make a person 'liable with his life' and so exempt from payment.

steps.title: מלקות remove כרת, according to רבי חנניה בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in מכות: anyone who deserved כרת and received מלקות is freed from כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned elsewhere: everyone who deserves כרת and received lashes is freed from their כרת. The verse says 'your brother will be dishonored before you'. Once he was flogged, he is like your brother. These are the words of רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from a different place. It says that receiving מלקות in court cancels the punishment of כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many sins that bring כרת are also punished with מלקות by a court. רבי חנניה בן גמליאל learns from the verse that once a person is flogged, he is 'your brother' again, so his sin is forgiven and כרת no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there (in a משנה elsewhere)
The תנא who says מלקות removes כרת

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת מכות.

phrases.english: All who are liable to karet who were flogged
are freed from their karet,
as it is said: "And your brother be dishonored before your eyes",
phrases.notes: This verse is about someone receiving lashes in court.

phrases.english: once he was flogged, he is like your brother.
These are the words of Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that will soon connect back to the משנה about שבת and יום הכפורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חנניה בן גמליאל, a person who deserves כרת and receives מלקות is freed from כרת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: his colleagues disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the other Sages disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: His colleagues disagree with him, with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds that רבי חנניה בן גמליאל's view is not accepted by everyone. His colleagues hold that מלקות does not remove כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבי חנניה בן גמליאל's statement into a dispute. The next step will show where this disagreement can be seen.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
His colleagues disagree with him
with Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲלוּקִין עָלָיו חֲבֵירָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds that the view in step 29 is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The other Sages hold that מלקות does not remove כרת.

steps.title: Proof from our משנה that the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: בי רב prove from our משנה that the Sages disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל, because otherwise יום הכפורים would also be punished by human hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The school of רב said: We already learned this. The only difference between יום הכפורים and שבת is that one is punished by people, and the other with כרת. If רבי חנניה בן גמליאל were right, both would be punished by people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי יוחנן's point using the משנה from step 25. That משנה says יום הכפורים is punished with כרת and not by people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking יום הכפורים on purpose can also bring מלקות from a court. If מלקות removed כרת, as רבי חנניה בן גמליאל says, the real punishment for יום הכפורים would be in human hands, just like שבת. Since the משנה says the difference is that יום הכפורים is כרת, it must not agree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned it (in a משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same משנה as step 25. The גמרא repeats it here on purpose to use it as a proof for a new question, not to explain it again.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is an attempt to support רבי יוחנן's report that the חכמים disagree. The next steps show the attempt does not hold up.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The school of Rav said:
We already learned it:
There is no difference between Yom Kippur and Shabbat
except that for this one, breaking it on purpose is punished by people,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is שבת, where a court gives the punishment.

phrases.english: and for that one, breaking it on purpose is punished with karet.
And if it were so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי חנניה בן גמליאל were right that lashes remove כרת.

phrases.english: both this and that would be punished by people!
phrases.notes: Because on יום הכפורים the court would give lashes, and that would replace the כרת.

steps.whatToRemember: בי רב try to prove from our משנה that the חכמים disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל. Steps 32-34 reject this proof.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב, תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings proof for רבי יוחנן's statement in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the Sages disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (step 25) saying the only difference is that שבת is punished by people and יום הכפורים with כרת.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The משנה follows רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects the proof of בי רב. He says our משנה follows רבי יצחק, who holds that sins punished by כרת never get מלקות at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי יצחק's, who says there are no מלקות for sins that carry כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on the proof of בי רב from Step 31. He says the משנה follows a Sage whose view makes the proof fall apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בי רב said that if מלקות can replace כרת, then יום הכפורים would have a punishment 'by human hands' too. But according to רבי יצחק, a sin punished by כרת can never get מלקות in the first place. So יום הכפורים only has כרת, and the משנה tells us nothing about the debate over רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A formula that names which Sage a teaching follows
People who are liable for כרת, being cut off by Heaven
There is not / does not exist

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying רבי חנניה בן גמליאל is wrong. He is only saying our משנה cannot prove anything about that debate.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yitzchak's,
who said: there are no lashes for those liable for karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי יִצְחָק הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of בי רב from Step 31 by assigning the משנה to רבי יצחק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from our משנה that the חכמים disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes that מלקות can apply to sins punished by כרת. רבי יצחק denies this, so the משנה would have no human-hands punishment for יום הכפורים anyway.

steps.title: The source for רבי יצחק's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יצחק learns from the separate mention of כרת for one's sister that sins punished by כרת get כרת and not מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יצחק says, all those liable for כרת were already included in the general rule. So why was כרת for one's sister stated separately? To punish her with כרת and not with מלקות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where רבי יצחק's view, quoted in Step 32, comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the forbidden relationships were already given כרת in one general פסוק. So when the תורה states כרת again, separately, for a man's sister, רבי יצחק says this teaches something new: the punishment is כרת and not מלקות. This serves as the model for every sin punished by כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
They were included in the general rule
Was taken out (stated separately from the general rule)

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
Those liable for karet were included in the general rule,
phrases.notes: The general rule is the פסוק in ויקרא 18 that gives כרת for any of these forbidden relationships.

phrases.english: so why was karet for one's sister stated separately?
phrases.notes: The sister is mentioned again with כרת in ויקרא 20, even though she was already covered.

phrases.english: To sentence her with karet and not with lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's claim in Step 32 by quoting the source of רבי יצחק's view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יצחק holds there are no מלקות for sins punished by כרת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יצחק reads the separate mention of כרת for one's sister as teaching כרת rather than מלקות.

steps.title: רב אשי: Even the רבנן can explain the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a second rejection of the proof. Even the רבנן, who allow מלקות for sins punished by כרת, can say the משנה is only describing the main punishment of each day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן. The main punishment for intentionally breaking this one (שבת) is by human hands, and the main punishment for intentionally breaking that one (יום הכפורים) is כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers another way to reject the proof of בי רב, without needing רבי יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if מלקות can apply to יום הכפורים, the main and original punishment for it is still כרת, while for שבת it is death by בית דין. The משנה is only contrasting the main punishments, so it says nothing against רבי חנניה בן גמליאל's view that someone who did get מלקות is freed from כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, here the Sages who disagree with רבי יצחק
By human hands, meaning punishment by בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: The proof of בי רב is rejected in two ways. רב נחמן says the משנה follows רבי יצחק (no מלקות for כרת at all). רב אשי says even the רבנן can read the משנה as describing only the main punishment of each day.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers show that our משנה cannot serve as proof for רבי יוחנן's report that the חכמים disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל, so the debate is not settled from here.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: These are the Sages who disagree with רבי יצחק and do give מלקות for sins punished by כרת.

phrases.english: this one: the main punishment for breaking it on purpose is by human hands,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is שבת.

phrases.english: and that one: the main punishment for breaking it on purpose is karet.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is יום הכפורים. If he did get lashes, he is freed from the כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent rejection of the proof from Step 31, without relying on רבי יצחק as Step 32 did.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof of בי רב, even according to the רבנן who allow מלקות for sins punished by כרת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the משנה lists every possible punishment. In fact it only contrasts the main punishment for each day.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה does not prove that the חכמים disagree with רבי חנניה בן גמליאל.
